methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: iHub open house invites community to explore innovation and technology - norfolkneradio.com
signals.signal_reading: Community-centered innovation spaces like iHub signal distributed capacity-building infrastructure in a non-NoVA region, creating peer learning networks that could foster grassroots AI fluency beyond metro concentration.

signals.title: News Flash Archive - NPD E911 Division implements Artificial Intelligence (AI) system on non-emergency lines - City of Norfolk (.gov)
signals.signal_reading: Municipal adoption of turnkey AI for E911 demonstrates shallow but practical platform deployment in public services—distributed geographically but not building deep local capability, as the system is likely vendor-managed rather than locally developed.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: AI creating workforce pressure on young workers without corresponding skill-building infrastructure suggests automation anxiety outpacing capability development—neither deep expertise nor broad fluency materializing fast enough to meet displacement risks.

signals.title: Norfolk's champion farm will show how AI can turn data into better crop decisions - EDP24
signals.signal_reading: Advanced agricultural AI for data-driven crop decisions represents deep technical application, but confined to champion farms with resources for adoption—concentrating precision agriculture capability rather than distributing it across Virginia's broader farming communities.

signals.title: UVA President Scott Beardsley charts University’s future in artificial intelligence - UVA Today
signals.signal_reading: UVA presidential focus on AI strategy concentrates research university resources and talent in Charlottesville, reinforcing the institutional advantage of established academic centers while rural regions remain dependent on knowledge transfer that may not materialize.
